papers.title: metaWEPP: leveraging biobank-scale intra-species phylogenies for near-haplotype resolution in metagenomic analysis.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic sequencing is transforming diverse areas of health and biological sciences, including pathogen surveillance, clinical diagnostics, and microbiome research. However, the inherent complexity of metagenomic data limits most computational tools to species-level classification and abundance estimation, overlooking within-species genetic diversity that drives key phenotypes. We present metaWEPP, a novel computational pipeline that achieves near-haplotype resolution in metagenomic analysis for species with adequate representation in reference genome biobanks and having sufficient sequenci
papers.summary: metaWEPP is a new computational pipeline that uses biobank-scale reference genomes to achieve near-haplotype resolution in metagenomic analysis, enabling the detection of within-species genetic diversity that is typically missed by species-level tools. This approach improves the ability to study strain-level variation in microbiomes, which is important for understanding phenotypes like pathogenicity and drug resistance.

papers.title: Dynamics of the magnum microbiome and predicted metabolic pathways across the egg-laying cycle in commercial laying hens.
papers.abstract: The microbiome of a chicken's reproductive tract is essential for egg production and safety. It helps regulate the immune system, preventing the transmission of pathogens like Salmonella and Staphylococcus that can contaminate eggs and pose health risks. Older hens may experience reduced immune function, which can disrupt their microbiome and increase the likelihood of harmful bacterial growth. We hypothesize that age-related shifts in the oviduct microbiome influence egg production and safety. This study aims to identify microbial communities and predicted pathways in the magnum of laying hen
papers.summary: This study investigates how the microbiome of the magnum (a section of the oviduct) changes with age in laying hens, and how these shifts may affect egg production and safety. The researchers identified specific microbial communities and predicted metabolic pathways that could influence the risk of pathogen transmission, such as Salmonella, into eggs. The findings suggest that age-related microbiome disruptions may compromise immune function and egg safety in older hens.

papers.title: Environmental emergence and dissemination of clinically relevant multidrug-resistant bacteria and resistance genes in sewage and aquatic ecosystems.
papers.abstract: This study characterized multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria in sewage, river, and marine ecosystems in South Gujarat, India.
papers.journal: Osong public health and research perspectives
papers.summary: This study characterized multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria in sewage, river, and marine ecosystems in South Gujarat, India, revealing widespread contamination with clinically relevant resistance genes. The findings highlight the role of aquatic environments as reservoirs and vectors for the spread of antibiotic resistance, underscoring the need for environmental surveillance.

papers.title: The need for standardization and improved open (meta)data practices in metaproteomics.
papers.abstract: Metaproteomics enables functional insight into microbial communities by identifying and quantifying proteins in complex samples. Yet, heterogeneous analytical workflows and the lack of standardization across experimental and bioinformatics stages hinder reproducibility and comparability, limiting integration with other omics data. We here present a community-developed reporting checklist tailored to the specific needs of metaproteomics. We also outline current efforts to enable structured and interoperable metadata capture, drawing on standards from proteomics and microbiome research wherever
papers.summary: This paper highlights the lack of standardization in metaproteomics workflows, which limits reproducibility and integration with other omics data. The authors present a community-developed reporting checklist and outline efforts to improve metadata capture by leveraging existing standards from proteomics and microbiome research.

papers.title: Molecular and phenotypic profiles of carbapenem- and third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from the fecal microbiota of pediatric patients with COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Gut colonization with multidrug-resistant (MDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae is commonly associated with an increased risk of extraintestinal infections among hospitalized patients. Extensive antibiotic exposure during the COVID-19 pandemic, is a critical contributing factor for the emergence of resistant strains. This investigation sought to elucidate the phenotypic and molecular resistance traits of carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) and extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing K. pneumoniae (ESBL-KP) colonizing the gut of pediatric patients with confirmed COVID-19.
papers.summary: This study found that pediatric COVID-19 patients had high rates of gut colonization with multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, including carbapenem-resistant and ESBL-producing strains, likely driven by extensive antibiotic use during the pandemic. The research highlights the need for antimicrobial stewardship in hospitalized children to prevent the spread of resistant infections.

papers.title: Causal Relationships Between Oral Microbiota and Inflammatory Skin Diseases.
papers.abstract: The oral microbiome has been increasingly linked to systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation, but whether specific oral bacteria causally contribute to inflammatory skin diseases remains unclear due to confounding and reverse causation. This study aimed to assess the causal effects of 43 oral microbiota taxa on the risk of five inflammatory skin diseases using a Mendelian randomization (MR) approach.
papers.summary: This study used Mendelian randomization to investigate whether specific oral bacteria causally influence the risk of inflammatory skin diseases, finding evidence for causal relationships between certain oral microbiota taxa and conditions like psoriasis and atopic dermatitis. The findings suggest that the oral microbiome may play a direct role in skin inflammation, independent of confounding factors.

papers.title: Maternal contact and age-dependent succession influence the assembly of the calf rumen microbiome and virome.
papers.abstract: Early-life colonization of the rumen is particularly important; however, the processes by which microbial and viral communities are transmitted and developed remain poorly understood. Here, we present a genome-resolved investigation of the effects of maternal contact and age-dependent succession on the calf rumen microbiome and DNA virome by comparing calves raised with or without maternal contact across early life using the metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) and viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) reconstructed from whole- and virus-like particle metagenomes. Across longitudinal sample
papers.summary: This study uses metagenome-assembled genomes and viral operational taxonomic units to show that both maternal contact and age-dependent succession shape the developing rumen microbiome and DNA virome in calves. Calves with maternal contact had different microbial and viral communities compared to those raised without, highlighting the importance of early-life transmission.

papers.title: Integrative multicohort analysis reveals consistent sex differences in gut microbiota of multiple sclerosis patients.
papers.abstract: Biological sex is a key determinant in the onset and progression of multiple diseases. In multiple sclerosis (MS), females exhibit higher disease prevalence, earlier onset, and more pronounced inflammatory activity, whereas males tend to experience a more severe neurodegenerative course, characterized by accelerated central nervous system damage and increased brain atrophy. The gut microbiome has emerged as a critical factor in MS, as its composition can either ameliorate or exacerbate disease progression. In this study, we aimed to identify reproducible sex-associated differences in gut micro
papers.summary: This study analyzed multiple cohorts of multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and found consistent sex-specific differences in gut microbiota composition, which may help explain the distinct disease courses observed between males and females. The findings suggest that the gut microbiome could be a key mediator of sex-based differences in MS progression.

papers.title: Environmental reservoirs and transmission pathways of antimicrobial resistance across the pork production continuum.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major One Health challenge linking human, animal, and environmental health, yet the contribution of food production environments to resistance transmission remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates how antimicrobial resistance (AMR) spreads through the entire pork production chain, from farms to processing plants, by analyzing environmental reservoirs and transmission pathways. The findings highlight that manure, soil, and water act as key reservoirs, with resistance genes persisting and potentially transferring to humans via food or environmental exposure. This work underscores the need for integrated One Health strategies to mitigate AMR in food systems.

papers.title: A Validated LC-MS/MS Method for Quantifying Phenolic Acids, Lignans, and Enterolignans from Human Fecal Samples.
papers.abstract: The human gut is home to numerous small molecules that impact health. Three prominent classes of molecules in this environment are phenolic acids, lignans, and enterolignans, which have been linked to anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects as well as protection from cancer, cardiovascular disease, and neurodegeneration. The abundance of these molecules in the intestine as well as their biological significance motivated the development and validation of the LC-MS/MS method reported herein, which provides a simple, robust, and high-throughput approach to simultaneously quantify a 22-membered
papers.summary: This paper presents a new LC-MS/MS method for simultaneously measuring 22 phenolic acids, lignans, and enterolignans in human fecal samples. The method is simple, robust, and high-throughput, enabling better study of these gut metabolites linked to anti-inflammatory and protective health effects.

papers.title: mBatchNet: an interactive web server for diagnosis, correction, and benchmarking of batch effects in microbiome data.
papers.abstract: Batch-effect diagnosis and correction are important for reproducible microbiome analysis and cross-study integration. Several batch-correction algorithms are available, but applying and comparing established methods in practice remains nontrivial because they differ in assumptions, accepted inputs, parameters, and evaluation outputs. Here, we present mBatchNet, an interactive web server for applying established batch-correction methods to processed microbiome feature tables and evaluating their effects within a single workflow. The server supports correction methods spanning recent microbiome-
papers.summary: mBatchNet is an interactive web server that simplifies the diagnosis, correction, and benchmarking of batch effects in microbiome data by integrating multiple established batch-correction methods into a single workflow. It addresses the challenge of comparing methods with different assumptions and inputs, making cross-study integration more accessible.

papers.title: Exploring differences in alveolar microbiome between pulmonary tuberculosis patients with different treatment outcomes: a metagenomic study from China.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate differences in the composition and functional characteristics of alveolar microbiota in patients with pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) exhibiting differential therapeutic responses. Thirty-two patients with drug-sensitive PTB who had completed standard anti-tuberculosis therapy were enrolled and classified into good-response (n = 16) and poor-response (n = 16) groups. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples were collected and analysed using metagenomic sequencing to characterize microbial community and functional pathways. No significant differences were observe
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing to compare the alveolar microbiome of pulmonary tuberculosis patients with good versus poor treatment outcomes, finding no significant differences in microbial composition or functional pathways between the two groups. The results suggest that the alveolar microbiome may not play a major role in differential treatment responses in drug-sensitive tuberculosis.

papers.title: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus OF44 alleviates allergic rhinitis by rebalancing host immunity and gut microbial function.
papers.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) involves a maladaptive type 2 inflammatory response driven by systemic immune imbalance and gut dysbiosis. Here, we identify a probiotic strain, Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus OF44, with significant probiotic potential that alleviates allergic pathology and is associated with coordinated immunological and microbial reprogramming. In an ovalbumin-induced AR rat model, OF44 administration markedly reduced nasal allergic symptoms, normalized serum and nasal immunoglobulin and cytokine levels, and restored the balance of Th1/Th2/Th17/Treg cell populations. Metagenomic profilin
papers.summary: This study identifies a probiotic strain, Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus OF44, that alleviates allergic rhinitis in rats by rebalancing immune responses (Th1/Th2/Th17/Treg) and restoring gut microbial function, suggesting a potential therapeutic approach for allergic rhinitis through gut-immune axis modulation.

papers.title: Viral genetic diversity and functional potential in polar and subarctic sea ice.
papers.abstract: Sea ice plays a critical role in regulating the global climate and serves as a unique habitat for diverse microbial communities. Still, our understanding of viruses in these communities remains limited. To further uncover the diversity and functional potential of viruses in polar and subarctic sea ice, we explored the viral component of Arctic, Baltic Sea, and Antarctic sea ice metagenomes. Altogether, 550 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) were recovered, most of which were putatively classified within the class Caudoviricetes, which comprises bacterial and archaeal tailed double-stran
papers.summary: This study analyzes metagenomes from Arctic, Baltic Sea, and Antarctic sea ice to uncover viral diversity, recovering 550 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs), mostly from the class Caudoviricetes. The findings expand our limited understanding of viruses in polar and subarctic sea ice ecosystems.

papers.title: Probiotics in pediatric functional abdominal pain disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Functional abdominal pain disorders (FAPDs), currently referred to as abdominal pain-related disorders of gut-brain interaction (AP-DGBIs), are characterized by recurrent abdominal discomfort in children that cannot be fully explained by an identifiable organic disorder. Probiotics are increasingly used as microbiota-targeted treatments, although their true clinical benefit remains uncertain. The objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of probiotic supplementation compared with placebo in children with AP-DGBIs. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and Scopus were searched fro
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of probiotics for treating functional abdominal pain disorders in children. The findings suggest that probiotics may offer some benefit, but the evidence is not strong enough to definitively recommend their routine clinical use.

papers.title: MicroWorldOmics: All-in-one Desktop Solution for Microbiome Profiling, Virome Analysis, and Unexplored "Dark Matter" Discovery.
papers.abstract: The large amount of high-throughput sequencing data generated in ecology, medicine, and pharmacology has increased the complexity of data analysis and interpretation. However, the microbiome and virome fields still lack a user-friendly and programming-free desktop application for comprehensive analysis of microbiome and virome data, with a particular gap in virome analysis and "dark matter" exploration. To address this gap, we introduce MicroWorldOmics, a plugin-based desktop application designed to offer a streamlined one-stop solution for life sciences and biomedical research. Its plugin-bas
papers.summary: MicroWorldOmics is a new desktop application that provides an all-in-one, user-friendly solution for analyzing microbiome and virome data without requiring programming skills. It fills a gap by including tools for virome analysis and exploring 'dark matter' sequences, making comprehensive analysis accessible to more researchers.

papers.title: First molecular detection of the genus Almendravirus in Johnbelkinia ulopus and Anopheles apicimacula mosquitoes from the Colombian Caribbean.
papers.abstract: Rhabdoviridae includes many viruses, among which rabies virus is notable. Other genera in this family can infect mammals, birds, reptiles, fish, and plants.
papers.summary: This study reports the first molecular detection of Almendravirus, a genus within the Rhabdoviridae family, in two mosquito species (Johnbelkinia ulopus and Anopheles apicimacula) from the Colombian Caribbean. The finding expands the known host range and geographic distribution of this virus genus, which is related to rabies virus but infects a variety of hosts.

papers.title: Fecal calprotectin and gut microbiome in a cohort without intestinal pathologies from northern Italy.
papers.abstract: Fecal calprotectin is a biomarker for intestinal inflammatory conditions, while specific taxa of gut microbiota are proposed as biomarkers for inflammatory bowel disease. However, the relationship between microbiota and calprotectin levels is still largely unexplored. Using shallow shotgun metagenomics, we investigate microbial taxonomic and functional patterns correlated with calprotectin levels in fecal samples of 515 adult individuals without known intestinal pathologies, enrolled within the Parma Microbiota Project. The median value of calprotectin was 23.6 μg/g, but levels higher than the
papers.summary: This study examines the relationship between fecal calprotectin levels and gut microbiome composition in 515 adults without known intestinal diseases from northern Italy. Using shallow shotgun metagenomics, the authors find that even within a healthy population, calprotectin levels correlate with specific microbial taxa and functional pathways, suggesting that subtle variations in this biomarker may reflect microbial changes independent of overt inflammation.

papers.title: The functional structure of foxtail millet rhizoplane microbiome and its association with yield.
papers.abstract: Root-associated microbial communities profoundly influence plant growth and productivity. Although the rhizosphere microbiome has been extensively studied, the functional distinctiveness and host-specific role of the closely adhering rhizoplane microbiota remain unclear. In this study, we performed deep metagenomic sequencing of both the rhizosphere and rhizoplane microbiomes in foxtail millet (Setaria italica). We constructed a comprehensive non-redundant gene catalog, reconstructed 595 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), and analyzed the co-occurrence networks. Our results revealed that the
papers.summary: This study used deep metagenomic sequencing to characterize the rhizoplane (root surface) microbiome of foxtail millet, constructing a gene catalog and 595 metagenome-assembled genomes. The rhizoplane microbiome was functionally distinct from the surrounding rhizosphere, and specific microbial features were associated with plant yield. This provides new insights into how closely adhering root microbes may influence crop productivity.

papers.title: Human skin microbiota and postpartum depression: A bidirectional Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a common mental health disorder after childbirth. Although microbiome research in PPD has mainly focused on the gut, the role of skin microbiota remains unclear. We used Mendelian randomization (MR) to assess potential causal associations between skin microbiota and PPD. A bidirectional 2-sample MR analysis used genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics. Genetic instruments for skin microbial features were obtained from a published skin microbiota GWAS, and PPD data were derived from 67,205 mothers (7604 cases, 59,601 controls). Instruments were sel
papers.summary: This study used Mendelian randomization to investigate whether skin microbiota composition is causally linked to postpartum depression (PPD). Analyzing genetic data from over 67,000 mothers, the authors found evidence for bidirectional causal relationships between certain skin microbial features and PPD risk. The findings suggest skin microbiota may play a role in PPD, expanding the focus beyond the gut microbiome.

papers.title: Personality-based subgroup identification and psychological symptom patterns in adolescent male new psychoactive substance users: implications for targeted intervention.
papers.abstract: Adolescent new psychoactive substance (NPS) users represent a high-risk population with complex psychological needs that remain insufficiently characterized, limiting the development of targeted rehabilitation interventions. This study aimed to (1) characterize the personality trait profiles and psychological symptom patterns of adolescent NPS users undergoing compulsory drug rehabilitation relative to normative standards; (2) identify empirically derived personality-based subgroups within this population; and (3) examine differential psychological symptom patterns across identified subgroups
papers.summary: This study profiles personality traits and psychological symptoms in adolescent male users of new psychoactive substances undergoing compulsory rehabilitation, identifying distinct personality-based subgroups with different symptom patterns. The findings suggest that tailored interventions could be developed based on these subgroup profiles to better address the complex psychological needs of this high-risk population.

papers.title: Human salivary microbiome as a potential non-invasive biomarker for early-onset colorectal cancer screening: a prospective study.
papers.abstract: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) has been increasing in recent years, the carcinogenesis of which has been linked to oral microbiota alterations. However, it is unknown if the salivary microbiome could help detect EOCRC. Therefore, we aimed to determine whether salivary microbiome profiles can distinguish patients with EOCRC from healthy individuals and to evaluate their diagnostic performance as a non-invasive screening tool.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the salivary microbiome can serve as a non-invasive biomarker for early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) screening. By comparing salivary microbiome profiles between EOCRC patients and healthy individuals, the researchers found distinct microbial signatures that could potentially distinguish the two groups, suggesting a promising new screening tool.

papers.title: Diversity and potential ecological roles of viruses in Pleistocene permafrost.
papers.abstract: Ancient permafrost, formed during past glacial periods, is widespread in Siberia and other Arctic regions. Even though these soils have remained below 0 °C over geological time periods, the widespread presence of bacteria and archaea in permafrost is well documented. However, the diversity of viruses in ancient permafrost of different geological ages and their potential ecological roles are still poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates the diversity of viruses in ancient permafrost from Siberia, revealing a wide variety of viral sequences across different geological ages. The findings suggest these viruses may play significant ecological roles in nutrient cycling and microbial community dynamics within the frozen soil.

papers.title: Metagenomics-based surveillance identifies possible sources of mastitis-associated organisms in organic and conventional dairy farm environments.
papers.abstract: Mastitis is one of the most economically significant diseases of the dairy industry. Although farm environments are recognized reservoirs for mastitis pathogens, comprehensive metagenomic comparisons between organic and conventional systems remain limited. We compared the prevalence, diversity, and functional potential of mastitis-associated organisms in one organic and one conventional dairy farm in Texas using shotgun metagenomics. Of 180 samples collected from six environmental sites (teats, liners, parlor floor mats, feed areas, bedding sands, and water troughs), 126 were retained after qu
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare mastitis-associated organisms in environmental samples from one organic and one conventional dairy farm. The findings highlight that farm environments serve as reservoirs for mastitis pathogens, with differences in prevalence and diversity between the two farming systems.

papers.title: Research Note: Exploratory analysis of temporal changes in ceca and plasma metabolite profiles of broiler chickens utilizing untargeted metabolomics.
papers.abstract: The gastrointestinal tract and its microbiota are researched for their impact on the health and performance of broiler chickens, which have been selected for rapid growth rate to meet demand. Untargeted metabolomics is one method that can potentially link changes in the gut microbiota to changes in metabolites and assist in revealing mechanisms affecting health outcomes. In this study, untargeted metabolomics via Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-MS) was performed to characterize changes in ceca and plasma metabolite profiles during early development (d 1, 3, and
papers.summary: This study uses untargeted metabolomics to track how metabolite profiles in the ceca and plasma of broiler chickens change during early development (days 1, 3, and beyond). The findings help link gut microbiota activity to metabolic shifts, potentially revealing mechanisms that affect chicken health and growth.

papers.title: Evaluating the impact of immunization with the "pan-fungal" vaccine, NXT-2, on the gut mycobiome and microbiome in non-human primates (NHPs).
papers.abstract: Fungal infections remain a significant public health concern with high mortality, morbidity, and increasing associated health costs. This burden is projected to rise due to expansion of at-risk populations, limited therapeutics, increasing drug resistance, and the emergence of new fungal pathogens. Even with these challenges, there are currently no approved vaccines. We previously developed a "pan-fungal" vaccine candidate, NXT-2, that confers protection against multiple invasive fungal infections such as pulmonary aspergillosis, pneumocystosis, and invasive candidiasis, as well as non-invasiv
papers.summary: This study evaluates the impact of the experimental pan-fungal vaccine NXT-2 on the gut mycobiome and microbiome in non-human primates, finding that immunization does not significantly disrupt these microbial communities. The results support the safety of NXT-2 as a vaccine candidate against multiple invasive fungal infections.

papers.title: Hawaiian geothermal fumaroles contain diverse and novel viruses.
papers.abstract: Viral community structure is known to influence the evolution of microbes in diverse and complex environments. While the diversity of microbes and their viruses have been metagenomically explored in terrestrial hot springs and hydrothermal vent systems, other volcanic features remain remarkably understudied. Fumaroles (steam vents) are geothermal features that heat groundwater with magma, releasing heated water vapor and volcanic gases, such as CO2 and H2S. Fumaroles are physicochemically dynamic compared to terrestrial hot springs-temperatures and gas emissions fluctuate rapidly with volcanic
papers.summary: This study reveals that Hawaiian geothermal fumaroles (steam vents) harbor a diverse and novel community of viruses, expanding our understanding of viral diversity in understudied volcanic environments. The findings suggest that these dynamic, gas-rich features host unique viral populations distinct from those found in more stable hot springs.

papers.title: Importance of methods selected for microbiome studies: State of the science and challenges.
papers.abstract: The microbiota has impact on virtually every aspect of poultry production, including performance, health, and food safety. It is therefore not surprising that considerable promise exists for the application of microbiota science in addressing current and future challenges faced across the poultry industry. Yet, methodological variation among poultry microbiota studies has had negative impact on reproducibility of findings, thereby slowing the application of effective microbiota-based solutions in a production setting. The experimental workflow in microbiota research involves many steps, rangin
papers.summary: This review highlights how methodological variation across poultry microbiome studies undermines reproducibility and slows the translation of microbiota-based solutions into production settings. The authors discuss the many steps in the experimental workflow that contribute to this variability.

papers.title: High throughput chromatographic ultra-purification of virus-like particles for downstream viromics.
papers.abstract: Virus-like particles (VLPs) are an abundant component of microbiomes with critical ecological roles such as population control through viral predation and horizontal gene transfer. Studying the collection of viruses in microbiomes (the virome) through metagenomics has provided important insights into the composition and functions of VLPs in different environments. However, the current gold-standard method for VLP purification, CsCl density gradient ultracentrifugation (CsCl), is low throughput, time consuming and suffers from biases which limits the ability to study viromes in larger sample se
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper presents a new high-throughput chromatographic method for purifying virus-like particles (VLPs) that overcomes the limitations of the current gold-standard CsCl density gradient ultracentrifugation, which is slow, low-throughput, and biased. The method enables faster, more scalable VLP purification for downstream viromics studies, potentially allowing larger-scale analyses of viral communities in microbiomes.

papers.title: Hierarchical Multi-Omics Trajectory Prediction for fecal microbiota transplantation: a novel machine learning framework for small-sample longitudinal multi-omics integration.
papers.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has emerged as a highly effective treatment for recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection and is being actively investigated for numerous other conditions. While multi-omics studies have revealed dynamic changes in microbial communities and host metabolism following FMT, existing approaches are primarily descriptive and lack the ability to model individual patient trajectories or identify early biomarkers of treatment response. Small-sample, multi-omics, longitudinal prediction presents unique computational challenges: high dimensionality ($p \gg n$),
papers.summary: This paper presents a novel machine learning framework designed to predict patient trajectories after fecal microbiota transplantation by integrating longitudinal multi-omics data from small sample sizes. The method addresses key computational challenges like high dimensionality and missing data, enabling early identification of treatment response biomarkers. This work advances personalized medicine for FMT by moving from descriptive analysis to predictive modeling.

papers.title: Mycobiome Simplification in Wheat Is Associated With the Pathogen Parastagonospora nodorum.
papers.abstract: Plant mycobiomes are essential to plant health, yet their assembly under biotic stressors such as pathogen infection remains poorly understood. Plant pathogens can influence microbial community composition through direct antagonism and suppression of host immune responses, potentially altering mycobiome composition in ways that could affect plant performance. We investigated how the wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) foliar mycobiome was associated with inoculation with the fungal pathogen Parastagonospora nodorum (Berk.) Quaedvlieg, Verkley & Crous, which can cause substantial loss of yield and gra
papers.summary: This study shows that infection of wheat leaves by the fungal pathogen Parastagonospora nodorum simplifies the leaf mycobiome, reducing fungal diversity and altering community composition. The findings suggest that pathogen-driven disruption of the mycobiome may have consequences for plant health beyond direct disease damage.

papers.title: Substrate-Driven Microbiome Assembly in Water Hyacinth Vermicompost: Combined 16S rRNA and Shotgun Metagenomics for Sustainable Agriculture.
papers.abstract: Substrate composition is a primary determinant of microbial succession and functional dynamics in vermicomposting systems. However, comparative insights into how biomass pre-treatment influences microbial architecture and how different sequencing approaches capture these changes remain limited. In this study, evaluation was carried out on microbial community structure and metabolic potential in vermicompost derived from three forms of Eichhornia crassipes (water hyacinth) biomass, burnt biomass (BB), composted biomass (CB) and dry biomass (DB) using both 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and s
papers.summary: This study investigates how different pre-treatments of water hyacinth biomass (burnt, composted, or dry) shape the microbial community and functional potential in vermicompost, using both 16S rRNA and shotgun metagenomics. The findings reveal that substrate composition drives distinct microbial architectures, with implications for optimizing vermicompost as a sustainable agricultural amendment.

papers.title: Comparing Accuracy and Biases of DNA Metabarcoding, Hybridization Capture, and Metagenomic Sequencing for Quantifying Herbivore Diets.
papers.abstract: DNA metabarcoding using relative read abundance (RRA) is commonly applied to estimate herbivore diet composition, yet its quantitative accuracy remains uncertain. We assessed taxonomic resolution and quantitative performance of RRA from DNA metabarcoding compared to metagenomic sequencing and hybridization capture, using deer scats from feeding trials and recreated diet samples using plant tissues. All methods recovered plant composition in recreated diets (R2 = 0.59-0.82), indicating accurate scaling with biomass in the absence of digestion, with only minor bias from amplicon length in DNA me
papers.summary: This study compares three DNA-based methods (metabarcoding, hybridization capture, and metagenomic sequencing) for quantifying herbivore diets from deer scat samples. All methods accurately estimated plant composition in recreated diets, with minor biases from amplicon length in metabarcoding, suggesting that relative read abundance can be a reliable proxy for diet quantification.

papers.title: Single-Thallus Genomics of Ejectosporus trisporus, an Unculturable Stonefly Gut Fungal Symbiont.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms play essential roles in global ecosystems, yet much of their diversity, particularly among fungi, remains unexplored due to challenges in culturing and genomic characterisation. Trichomycetes, an early-diverging lineage of obligate gut symbionts of aquatic insects, exemplify this 'microbial dark matter', as most taxa cannot be maintained in axenic culture. Here, we present the first culture-independent genome assembly of Ejectosporus trisporus, an unculturable Harpellales fungus isolated from the hindgut of a winter stonefly (Allocapnia sp.) in Rouge National Urban Park, Canada.
papers.summary: This study presents the first culture-independent genome assembly of Ejectosporus trisporus, an unculturable fungal symbiont from the hindgut of a stonefly, overcoming challenges in genomic characterization of such 'microbial dark matter'. The work provides a valuable genomic resource for understanding the biology and evolution of obligate gut symbionts in aquatic insects.

papers.title: Benchmarking DNA extraction protocols across use cases for culture-independent Nanopore metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing offers several advantages for metagenomics, including long reads, rapid turnaround, low upfront cost, scalability and portability. However, for ONT metagenomics, DNA yield, quality and integrity are important considerations when selecting an extraction method. Many metagenomic extraction methods use harsh lysis conditions to extract a wide range of species and provide an accurate community composition, but these conditions can compromise DNA fragment length. Therefore, extraction methods for ONT metagenomics must balance DNA shearing and recovery w
papers.summary: This study systematically compares DNA extraction protocols for Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) metagenomics, finding that methods must balance DNA yield and fragment length to achieve accurate community composition. The authors provide practical recommendations for selecting extraction methods based on specific use cases, such as rapid turnaround or high-molecular-weight DNA.

papers.title: Revalorizing Cocoa Endocarp Residues as Novel Ingredients With Potential Prebiotic Effects: A Step Toward Circular Economy.
papers.abstract: The interior part of the cocoa husk, known as the cocoa endocarp, is a by-product of the chocolate sector that contains bioactive compounds with health benefits. In this research, the nutritional and physicochemical characteristics, and antioxidant capacity of dehydrated (DC) and lyophilized (LC) cocoa endocarps were evaluated, as well as their prebiotic properties affecting the human intestinal microbiota (IM). A simulated gastrointestinal digestion process was applied to DC and LC prior to 48 h of in vitro fecal fermentation. An increase in the relative abundance (RA) of beneficial intestina
papers.summary: This study shows that cocoa endocarp, a byproduct of chocolate production, can be processed into a food ingredient with prebiotic potential. After simulated digestion and fermentation, both dehydrated and lyophilized cocoa endocarp increased beneficial gut bacteria, suggesting it could be used to promote gut health while reducing food waste.

papers.title: Structural Characterization and Gut Microbiota Modulation of Theabrownins Prepared by Macroporous Resin AB-8 Combined With Ultrafiltration Fractionation.
papers.abstract: This study developed an efficient and environmentally benign method using macroporous resin purification combined with ultrafiltration fractionation to prepare a high-molecular-weight theabrownin fraction (TBSP5, Mw > 100 kDa) from summer green tea fermented with Aspergillus cristatus (MK346334). TBSP5 exhibited higher purity than theabrownins obtained via conventional organic solvent extraction (TBSE) while it retained comparable structural characteristics. Both TBSP5 and TBSE showed substantial stability under simulated upper gastrointestinal digestion, undergoing only limited hydrolysis bef
papers.summary: This study developed a greener method using macroporous resin and ultrafiltration to purify high-molecular-weight theabrownins from fermented tea, yielding a purer product than conventional solvent extraction. The purified theabrownins remained stable during simulated digestion, suggesting potential for gut microbiota modulation.

papers.title: Metabolic Syndrome Is Associated With Increased Risk of Clostridioides difficile Infection Diagnosis and Severe Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a major cause of antibiotic-associated diarrhea in the United States. Gut dysbiosis and chronic inflammation are key contributors to CDI susceptibility and severity. Metabolic syndrome (MetS)-defined by central obesity, hypertriglyceridemia, low HDL cholesterol, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)-is increasingly prevalent worldwide and is characterized by chronic immune dysregulation and alterations in gut microbiota. These pathophysiologic features may overlap with mechanisms that predispose individuals to CDI and its complications.
papers.summary: This study finds that metabolic syndrome (a cluster of conditions like obesity, high blood pressure, and diabetes) is associated with a higher risk of developing C. difficile infection and experiencing severe outcomes. The overlap between metabolic syndrome's chronic inflammation and gut microbiome changes may explain this increased susceptibility.

papers.title: Analysis of Gut Microbiota Metabolites in Chronic Kidney Disease-Associated Pruritus Using Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus (CKD-aP) remains a frequent and distressing symptom in patients with renal dysfunction, yet its biological mechanisms are still not well defined. Growing evidence suggests that gut microbiota-derived metabolites may participate in systemic inflammatory regulation, providing a potential entry point for exploring CKD-aP pathogenesis.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular docking to investigate how gut microbiota metabolites might contribute to chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus (CKD-aP). The findings suggest that specific microbial metabolites could influence systemic inflammation pathways relevant to CKD-aP, offering new insights into its underlying mechanisms.

papers.title: In silico dysbiosis-associated neuroprotective metabolite insufficiency in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Perturbation of oral and gut microbiomes has been implicated in alzheimer's disease (AD) along the oral-gut-brain axis; however, the extent of global community restructuring may differ between niches. The present work constitutes a computational interrogation of 16S rRNA profiles from eight-month-old APP/PS1 and wild-type mice, characterizing oral and gut community structure and predicted functional capacity through PICRUSt-driven, KEGG-anchored pathway inference. Comparative taxonomic interrogation disclosed patterns consistent with ectopic occurrence, whereby classically oral genera (Fusobac
papers.summary: This study uses computational analysis of 16S rRNA data from Alzheimer's disease model mice to show that oral and gut microbiomes are disrupted, with oral bacteria appearing in the gut. The predicted functional changes suggest a deficiency in neuroprotective metabolites, potentially linking microbiome dysbiosis to Alzheimer's pathology.

papers.title: Functional signatures of the gut microbiome in middle-aged regular runners: insights from a metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Exercise influences host metabolism and inflammation, but its functional effects on the gut microbiome in middle-aged populations remain unclear. This study used shotgun metagenomics to investigate the associations between long-term endurance running and the gut microbial ecosystem and its functional potential in middle-aged adults.
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the gut microbiomes of middle-aged regular runners versus non-runners, finding that long-term endurance running is associated with distinct functional signatures in the gut microbial ecosystem. The results suggest that regular exercise may promote a healthier gut microbiome composition and metabolic potential in middle-aged adults.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of fecal and environmental microbiota in rural mixed livestock farming systems in South Africa.
papers.abstract: In South African rural areas, farmers often practice mixed extensive livestock farming, facilitating microbial exchange among and between animal species and their environment. The composition and transmission potential of microbiomes between animals and their environments in these smallholder livestock systems remain largely unexplored, creating a gap in understanding how mixed-livestock farming affects gut and environmental microbiomes. Shotgun metagenomics was used to uncover the fecal and environmental microbiota in smallholder mixed livestock systems, aiming to understand microbiome transf
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomics to characterize the fecal and environmental microbiomes in smallholder mixed livestock farms in rural South Africa, revealing microbial exchange between animals and their surroundings. The findings fill a gap in understanding how mixed-livestock farming shapes microbiome composition and transmission potential in these understudied systems.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in soil microbiome-driven agriculture: from practical limits to a translational roadmap.
papers.abstract: Soil microbiome research has been revolutionized by advances in high-throughput sequencing and multi-omics technologies, generating massive datasets that capture the taxonomic, functional, and metabolic diversity of microbial communities in agricultural soils; however, interpreting these complex datasets and translating them into practical agronomic insights remains challenging.
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence can help analyze large soil microbiome datasets to improve agriculture, but also highlights current limitations and proposes a roadmap for translating these insights into practical farming applications.

papers.title: The Gut-Joint Axis in Hip Osteoarthritis: Distinct Articular Microbial Profiles and Metabolic Potential Compared With Nonarthritic Controls.
papers.abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis and systemic microbial translocation potentially contribute to chronic joint inflammation. However, the role of the gut-joint axis in the genesis of osteoarthritis still needs to be elucidated. This investigation characterized taxonomic signatures and proinflammatory metabolic pathways within the hip joint to define their contribution to the pathophysiology of osteoarthritis relative to nonarthritic controls.
papers.summary: This study found distinct microbial profiles and metabolic pathways in the hip joints of osteoarthritis patients compared to nonarthritic controls, suggesting that gut-derived microbes may contribute to joint inflammation. The findings support the existence of a gut-joint axis in osteoarthritis, where intestinal dysbiosis could drive chronic joint pathology.

papers.title: Shared and condition-associated gut microbiota alterations in older adults with depression and constipation: evidence from the American Gut Project.
papers.abstract: Constipation and depression frequently co-occur in older adults, and growing evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis may be a shared feature of both conditions. The microbiota has well-established roles in gastrointestinal motility and gut-brain axis signaling, and compositional alterations have been independently reported in each condition. However, whether older adults with constipation and those with depression share common microbiota characteristics have not been systematically investigated.
papers.summary: This study analyzed gut microbiota data from older adults in the American Gut Project and found shared microbial alterations in those with depression and constipation, suggesting a common dysbiosis pattern. The findings highlight potential gut-brain axis mechanisms linking these co-occurring conditions in aging populations.

papers.title: Age-associated gut microbiome succession, colonization resistance, and relative resistome patterns in an antibiotic-restricted infant cohort.
papers.abstract: Early infancy is critical for gut microbiome assembly and the establishment of colonization resistance against pathobionts. Whether age-associated microbiome maturation is accompanied by changes in colonization-resistance proxies and relative antimicrobial resistance gene profiles under low infant antibiotic exposure remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study examines how the gut microbiome matures in infants with minimal antibiotic exposure, finding that age-related changes in microbial communities are linked to increased colonization resistance against harmful bacteria and shifts in antimicrobial resistance gene profiles. The results suggest that natural microbiome succession in early life can enhance protective functions even without antibiotic pressure.

papers.title: Fecal metagenomic profiling in patients with colorectal adenomas to characterize gut microbial composition and functional potential.
papers.abstract: To investigate differences in gut microbiota between patients with colorectal adenoma (CRA) and healthy individuals using metagenomic sequencing, and to analyze the correlation between microbial abundance and polyp diameter and number.
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing to compare the gut microbiota of patients with colorectal adenomas (precancerous polyps) to healthy individuals, finding distinct microbial compositions and functional potentials. The abundance of certain bacteria correlated with polyp size and number, suggesting that gut microbes could serve as biomarkers for early detection of colorectal cancer risk.

papers.title: Microbial functional gene assembly is associated with soil carbon and nitrogen dynamics during grassland degradation.
papers.abstract: Grassland degradation is often accompanied by changes in the structure and function of soil microbial communities. However, the mechanisms by which the assembly of microbial functional communities is associated with alterations in soil carbon and nitrogen pools remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the assembly of microbial functional genes relates to changes in soil carbon and nitrogen pools during grassland degradation. The findings reveal that shifts in microbial functional gene composition are closely linked to alterations in soil carbon and nitrogen dynamics, providing insights into the ecological consequences of grassland degradation.

papers.title: In silico identification and biophysical characterization of candidate antimicrobial peptides from the Indian marine microbiome targeting multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens.
papers.abstract: The global health crisis of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the discovery of new antibacterial agents. Underexplored marine microbiomes, particularly from the biodiverse Indian coast, represent a rich potential source of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). Targeting the urgent threat of multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens, the present study aimed to computationally identify novel, membrane-active AMPs from these unique metagenomic datasets, with a focus on inhibiting Gram-negative bacteria. In this study, we computationally mined Indian marine high-resolution shotgun metagenomic datasets thr
papers.summary: This study computationally identified novel antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) from Indian marine metagenomic datasets, targeting multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens. The authors used in silico screening and biophysical characterization to find membrane-active AMPs with potential against Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting underexplored marine microbiomes as a source of new antibiotics.

papers.title: Domestication reshapes the swine gut microbiome: metagenomic insights into taxonomic and functional divergence across wild and domestic populations.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota constitutes a highly diverse, complex, and dynamically evolving ecosystem within the host. However, the domestication process may alter microbial community composition and function. Here, we investigate these shifts using metagenomic analysis.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic analysis to compare the gut microbiomes of wild and domestic swine, revealing that domestication has significantly altered both the taxonomic composition and functional potential of the gut microbiota. These findings provide insights into how host lifestyle and environment shape microbial communities.

papers.title: Next-generation soil monitoring: linking metagenomics, biosensors, and ecological modeling for sustainable agriculture.
papers.abstract: Soils represent one of the most complex and dynamic biological systems on Earth, where microbial communities play a central role in regulating ecosystem functions, including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, and plant productivity. However, increasing pressures from land-use intensification and climate change threaten soil health and biodiversity, highlighting the need for innovative monitoring and management approaches. In this review, we synthesize current advances in soil microbial ecology, sustainable soil management, environmental sensing technologies, and metagenomics to propose an
papers.summary: This review proposes an integrated framework combining metagenomics, biosensors, and ecological modeling to monitor soil health and microbial communities for sustainable agriculture. The authors synthesize advances in soil microbial ecology and environmental sensing to address threats from land-use intensification and climate change.

papers.title: Cervical Cytological Findings and Vaginal Microbiota Alterations During Pregnancy: A Retrospective Analysis.
papers.abstract: Pregnancy induces physiological and microbiological changes in the cervicovaginal environment, which may affect the interpretation of cervical cytology. Accurate screening in this population is essential to identify both benign and pathological alterations.
papers.summary: This retrospective study examines how pregnancy alters the vaginal microbiota and cervical cytology findings, which can complicate screening interpretation. The authors emphasize the need for accurate screening to distinguish benign pregnancy-related changes from true pathological alterations.

papers.title: Tripterygium glycosides tablet ameliorates chronic kidney disease via gut-derived uremic toxins reduction in rats: alkaloids as major toxic ingredients.
papers.abstract: Tripterygium glycosides tablet (TGT), the major preparation of Tripterygium wilfordii Hook. f (TWHF), is widely used in treating chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, its complex composition and overlap between active and toxic constituents often lead to adverse effects, limiting precise clinical use. This study aimed to clarify the therapeutic mechanisms of TGT in CKD and identify its potential toxic ingredients.
papers.summary: This study shows that Tripterygium glycosides tablets (TGT) improve chronic kidney disease in rats by reducing gut-derived uremic toxins, and identifies alkaloids as the primary toxic components. The findings help separate therapeutic benefits from adverse effects, potentially guiding safer clinical use of TGT.

papers.title: Clinical and immunomicrobiome correlates of a standardized Qingpao Chushi Jiedu Fang regimen in palmoplantar pustulosis.
papers.abstract: Palmoplantar pustulosis (PPP) is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis with limited therapeutic options. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulations may benefit PPP, yet microbiome-immune mechanisms underlying clinical response remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates how a Traditional Chinese Medicine formula (Qingpao Chushi Jiedu Fang) affects palmoplantar pustulosis by analyzing changes in the skin microbiome and immune markers. The findings suggest that clinical improvement correlates with shifts in microbial composition and immune responses, offering potential mechanistic insights into TCM-based treatment for this chronic skin condition.

papers.title: Immune dysregulation drives the relapse of peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis: a single-center prospective study.
papers.abstract: The diagnosis and management of relapsing peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis (PDAP) remains a clinical challenge. This study aimed to identify biomarkers associated with relapsing PDAP and discuss potential mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study identifies immune dysregulation as a key driver of relapsing peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis (PDAP), highlighting potential biomarkers for diagnosis and management. The findings suggest that specific immune factors may predict relapse, offering new targets for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Relationships of oxidative stress, inflammation and gut microbiota with cognitive impairment in first-episode major depressive disorders: a pilot study in China.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment runs through the entire course of major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the relationships between cognitive impairment and the gut microbiota (GM) and their predicted metabolic pathways as well as peripheral blood indicators remains unclear. We aimed to explore these relationships.
papers.summary: This pilot study in China found that first-episode MDD patients with cognitive impairment had altered gut microbiota composition and predicted metabolic pathways, along with increased oxidative stress and inflammation markers in blood. The findings suggest that gut-brain axis disruptions involving oxidative stress and inflammation may contribute to cognitive deficits in early-stage depression.

papers.title: Longitudinal changes in oral conditions and oral candidiasis in palliative care inpatients: a longitudinal observational study.
papers.abstract: Oral health influences comfort, communication, and quality of life in palliative care. However, its clinical drivers and prognostic significance remain poorly understood. This study examined longitudinal changes in oral conditions over time and identified factors associated with oral deterioration or improvement.
papers.summary: This study tracked changes in oral health over time in palliative care inpatients, finding that oral conditions often worsen and that oral candidiasis is a common issue. The research identifies key factors linked to oral deterioration, which could help clinicians better manage symptoms and improve patient comfort.

papers.title: Association between the subcellular localization of host proteins and gut microbiome and metabolome in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is estimated to affect 38% of the global population, with limited options for treatment. It could progress to metabolic-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Agonists for farnesoid X receptor (FXR), peroxisome proliferation-associated receptors (PPARs), and sirtuin1 (SIRT1) are currently investigated for MASLD treatment. The subcellular localization of those proteins was shown to affect their function and could possibly be affected by different metabolites. Moreover, while those protein target
papers.summary: This pilot study investigates how the subcellular localization of host proteins (FXR, PPARs, SIRT1) relates to gut microbiome composition and metabolome in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). The findings suggest that changes in protein localization may be influenced by microbial metabolites, offering potential insights into MASLD pathogenesis and treatment targets.
